John W. Campbell, Islands of Space.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/john-w-campbell/islands-of-space

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- John W. Campbell, the author and annotator, died 1971 (Wikidata Q435056, P570 = 1971-07-11).

First publication of the text used: 1931 (SE colophon: 'Islands of Space was published in 1931 by John W. Campbell').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1931 (SE colophon), which is after 1930, so this bullet relies on Standard Ebooks' statement of rights quoted below.
- Country of origin (United States): the novel first appeared in the American magazine Amazing Stories Quarterly in spring 1931 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islands_of_Space). Its first book edition came out in 1957 from Fantasy Press of Reading, Pennsylvania (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fantasy_Press). The origin is the United States, the same country as the bullet above, so no other country's term applies.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: Islands of Space was published in 1931 by John W. Campbell.
- Wikidata Q435056 (John W. Campbell), P570 = 1971-07-11; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_W._Campbell
